ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows two hemispheric maps with latitude and longitude grids, marking the locations of multiple cities. The left figure shows the Asia–Oceania region, marked with cities such as “Beijing” and “Singapore,” and the figure also shows city points near Australia; the right figure marks cities on the Americas side, such as “Rio de Janeiro.” The latitude and longitude grid can be used to judge the longitudinal positions of the cities relative to Beijing. Then reason: The question stem states that the “Earth Hour” activity began with lights being turned off at 20:30 local time. The day of the activity was March 23, close to the spring equinox, when the lengths of day and night are nearly equal, so Beijing’s sunset time can be approximately regarded as around 18:00 local time. If, when the sun set in Beijing, a certain city was just beginning to turn off its lights, then the local time in that city was about 20:30, about 2.5 hours ahead of Beijing in entering the night time, that is, the local time was about 2.5 hours faster than Beijing time. The Earth rotates through 15° of longitude per hour, and 2.5 hours corresponds to about 37.5° of longitude. Beijing is around 116°E, and about 37.5° eastward is around 150°E. Combining the latitude and longitude grid and the distribution of cities in the figure, the area near 150°E corresponds to eastern Australia. Therefore, this city was most likely located in Australia.

Since the date is near the equinox, take Beijing sunset as about 18:00 local solar time. The target city must therefore be about 2.5 hours ahead of Beijing, i.e. about 37.5° farther east. Use the map grid to move eastward from Beijing's longitude to roughly 150°E; the marked city/area there is in Australia. Conclude the country is Australia.
